key_insight: A dual-resonator silver microcavity can simultaneously boost sensitizer absorption and directional emission in solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical optical-cavity strategy to improve sub-bandgap light harvesting for more efficient photovoltaic and low-intensity optoelectronic devices.
method: Thermally co-evaporated a rubrene:PdPC active layer inside a planar silver microcavity.
Aligned one dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at 32° to enhance sensitizer absorptance.
Used a second cavity mode to out-couple upconverted emission while balancing reabsorption losses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 12-fold absorptance enhancement at 665 nm, a 22-fold peak increase in detected upconversion emission, and a 4.5-fold improvement when integrated over the emission band.
watch_item: Performance depends on precise cavity-mode alignment and may be sensitive to reabsorption, aggregation quenching, and fabrication tolerances.
paper_title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
